Regenerate with: just gen-policy (dhall-to-json --pretty --file policy/dhall/delegation.dhall); dhall-json ships in the flake dev shell. Degraded mode when dhall-to-json is off PATH: hand-sync this file to the Dhall byte-for-byte, per the lab test/dhall convention. Document shape is described by policy/delegation.schema.json. Invariants enforced by tests/test_delegation_policy.py.

attribution.convention: Attribute every synthesis/recon session to a lane in session notes, following lab docs/agent-notes/INDEX.md.

budget_fallbacks.trigger: Opus 5.5 subagent quota is exhausted for the current window.

broker.notes: New policy in TIN-7125: the v0.4.0 kimi-never-gates rule had no clause about naming a model. Kimi k3.1-pro on Cade's broker seat routes a request to a cade.* lane and authors the cade.dispatch/v1 envelope. It gates nothing. It never names a model: the envelope has no model field, and the dispatch resolver picks the root from the lane and tags. Cade's own code stamps job_id, parent_job_id, depth, root_id, custody, requested_by and created_at. Custody comes from the source item's label, never from Kimi. Kimi may broker unattended: Jess ruled "all accounts are checked and suitable for Cade." (TIN-7125 0a1924b3).

children.notes: Cade's children are auto-level workers, like a fresh harness with bypass permissions and subagents (SPR-144). They are not read-only. Standing rules still bind them: external acts go through the daily batch confirm (BIZ-5) or Jess's confirm (CORE-5), health data is never hosted (SP-4), client raw exports stay in the confidential home or on Opus and never reach Kimi (SPR-102), ownership and live-session checks precede any signal (R-N11) and hook rulings stay advisory (R-N12). A child's custody class follows its parent home, so confidential-home children never route to Kimi. A child's effective seats are its lane's default and alternate seats that also sit in its parent home's custody class. When none remain, the child waits. A child never reroutes to another provider when its seat is unavailable: it waits.

cade.cross_provider_review: Advisory (SPR-145). Consequential Cade output may get a review on cade.review from the provider other than its author's. Cross-provider review is advisory evidence. It never blocks, never gates a merge and never stands in for Jess's approval or a batch confirm. A same-provider review is recorded as same-provider.

custody_classes.notes: Confidential-home work, including client raw exports and confidential papers. Opus 5.5 or on-prem only. Never Kimi.
Health data is never hosted (SP-4). It stays on-prem, no seat in this policy serves it and no cade.* lane carries it.
Non-confidential operating work. Opus 5.5 or Kimi K3.1 Pro. Every Kimi seat gets this class, the pi-k3 harness seat included (SPR-182). The claude-code@cade job seat also sees ops data.
Public-home work over public or synthetic material. Opus 5.5 or Kimi K3.1 Pro. The claude-code@cade job seat also sees public data.

accounting.notes: Every receipt records lineage, the model that answered each unit, children, peak concurrency, observed depth, tokens, wall time, effects and GO refs. The budget envelope is report-only: the card posts status lines at 50, 80 and 100 percent, and nothing stops. Nothing in dispatch caps subagent count, depth or cost, because a cap is containment and needs a ruled interview. Extra jobs queue first come, first served. An audit finding is a warning on the card, never a denial (R-N12).

credentials.notes: Jess signs in to cade@xoxd.ai, attended, under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude-cade on sting. It is a third cade@xoxd.ai sign-in, beside the two Hermes homes.
Cade's own Linear identity. Jess creates it in Linear's UI, and its custody row is written with the mint. Jobs comment as Cade, never as Jess.
A Cade GitHub App installation or token. Jess creates it in GitHub's UI, and its custody row is written with the mint. Jobs push to forks and open PRs as Cade.

effects.notes: The job writes only its result doc and receipt.
A result doc in a git-tracked cade-work notes path. Its {path, sha256} returns over swb.
A Linear comment under Cade's own Linear identity.
A branch pushed to a fork and a pull request opened under Cade's own GitHub identity. Cade never reviews her own PR and never merges it.
Any spend waits for Jess's confirm (CORE-5).
A send outside the estate waits for the daily batch confirm (BIZ-5) or Jess's confirm (CORE-5).
Each host act waits for its own GO from Jess (R-C754).
A merge of Cade's PR waits for an independent Opus review on mythos.gate.review and a GO.
Minting or rotating a credential is Jess's act. A job never does it.

fable_model_id.notes: Jess said "fable 5.2" and that id is not verified. After Jess's attended login under the job seat's config dir, the id is read from the account's model list, written to the job seat's dispatch config as fable_model_id and recorded on TIN-7125. Until then a Fable-root job waits and replies needs-go. The id never lands in this policy or in the provider allow-list. A read id must match id_pattern, so an Opus or Sonnet id cannot stand in for Fable.

job_seat.notes: Jess ruled "Under your own user on sting" (TIN-7125 0a1924b3). Jobs run as jess on sting with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude-cade, signed in to cade@xoxd.ai. There is no separate Unix user for jobs. Jess's own ~/.claude login is never used for a job. Jobs can reach Jess's keys, become file and gh login, and Jess accepted that. A job acts under Cade's own credentials, never under Jess's.

dispatch.notes: Cade Dispatch v1 (TIN-7125 e539eb42, 5c0eb819, 8cca9101 and 0a1924b3). Kimi brokers, and a fixed resolver picks the root. Jobs travel over swb to claude:sting:cade-jobs, where a receiver calls the fixed cade-job launcher. Replies carry kind reply, needs-go or dispatch-request. A tag matches a carve-out tag after lowercasing and dropping every character outside a-z and 0-9, and a tag that starts with a carve-out tag matches too. Inside a job the carve-out holds through named Opus agent definitions, advisory warnings and receipt audit, because hooks never deny (R-N12). No dispatch lane admits confidential or health custody in v1.

Code that may merge, tests and security-sensitive changes.
Gates and reviews inside the job. None of them gates a merge.

cade.orchestrator: Cade is an orchestrator, not a seat and not the operator. It decomposes business, marketing and CEO-ops work into cade.* lanes, picks each lane's seat from its default and permitted alternates within the lane's custody class, spawns children to run them and collects a receipt per child. Cade's code work follows CORE-5, and J81 governs the mythos.* lanes.

enforcement.rule: A lane whose persona is adversarial must never resolve to a persona that includes fable in its model classes.
The fable persona must forbid adversarial-analysis, purple-team, red-team, deep-iteration-hammering, and bulk-execution.
Every persona and lane carries a non-empty purpose string; routes self-document why, not just what.

A lane whose persona is critical or adversarial resolves to Opus 5.5 by default or to the operator personally. Those personas never list sonnet, haiku or fable in their model classes. A merge-gating review runs on Opus. mythos.review and harness reviews never gate a merge.

When Opus quota is exhausted, Sonnet may continue mythos.implement.merge and mythos.gate.security under the opus-quota-exhausted fallback. Merges from those lanes wait for an Opus review. The downgraded lane never runs a host act or a credential change. The downgrade is recorded in the receipt. The fallback never reaches mythos.gate.review, mythos.act.host or the adversarial persona: that work waits for Opus or goes to the operator. It never reaches fable or haiku. This narrows J81(e) on purpose to keep J81(a).

Every seat names a provider listed in providers. A seat's model_id must be on its provider's allow-list. Anthropic seats stay on the 5.5 family and fable stays provider-managed. A seat that names an endpoint runs only on an admitted endpoint whose model_ids hold its model_id. The kimi seat runs k3.1-pro on the kimi-coding endpoint through the Kimi Code subscription. The Platform endpoint and any Platform key are forbidden. A provider, endpoint or model id outside the allow-list fails closed.

The kimi seat never gates a merge. It never owns the refutation-of-record, never carries the operator WORD leg and never runs a critical host act. The critical and adversarial personas never list kimi. Kimi authors only on cade.* lanes that name it as a default or alternate seat. No mythos.* lane resolves to a persona that lists kimi.

A child's custody class follows its parent home. A child's effective seats are its lane's default and alternate seats that also sit in its parent home's custody class. When none remain, the child waits. Confidential work runs on Opus or on-prem only and never routes to Kimi. Public and ops work runs on Opus or Kimi. Health data is never hosted. Every seat a cade.* lane names sits in its custody class and in its persona's model classes. Fable serves only cade.delegate.*, as orchestrator: no route in cade.lanes names it.

Cade's children are auto-level workers, not read-only. Standing rules still bind them: external acts go through the daily batch confirm or Jess's confirm, health data is never hosted, client raw exports never reach Kimi, ownership and live-session checks precede any signal and hook rulings stay advisory. A child never reroutes to another provider when its seat is unavailable: it waits.
Cross-provider review is advisory evidence. It never blocks, never gates a merge and never stands in for Jess's approval or a batch confirm.

Fable leads, others work (TIN-7125 0a1924b3). A Fable root plans, picks each unit's model and synthesizes. It never runs a unit itself. Workers are Sonnet or Haiku for research and bulk work, and Opus for code, gates and every carve-out unit at any depth. Bulk execution stays forbidden to fable.

A fixed resolver, not the broker, picks a dispatched job's root seat from its lane and tags. cade.delegate.research, cade.delegate.draft, cade.delegate.business and cade.delegate.marketing get a Fable root as orchestrator. cade.delegate.develop gets an Opus root. Any carve-out tag on any lane reroutes the root to Opus. Uncertain or missing tags on cade.delegate.develop resolve to Opus. A lane that does not admit the job's custody gets no root, and the job does not run.

Carve-out tags pass to every child, at any depth. A unit or child job that carries a carve-out tag runs on Opus. Inside a job the carve-out holds through named Opus agent definitions, advisory warnings and receipt audit, because hooks never deny.
Custody comes from the source item's label, never from the broker. A child's custody stays the same as its parent's or narrows, in the order public, ops, confidential, health. It never widens.

New policy (TIN-7125). Kimi on the broker seat may route a request to a cade.* lane and author cade.dispatch/v1 envelopes. It gates nothing and never names a model: the envelope has no model field and the resolver picks the root. The broker never sets custody. Kimi may broker unattended (TIN-7125 0a1924b3).

The Fable model id is a config value read from the cade@xoxd.ai account after Jess's attended login. This policy never carries it. A Fable-root job waits until the id is read. A receipt whose observed root model differs from its resolved root model is an audit finding.
A Cade job never reviews a pull request that Cade opened. The merge gate for a Cade PR is an independent Opus review on mythos.gate.review.

Every receipt records lineage, observed models, children, peak concurrency, observed depth, tokens, wall time, effects and GO refs. The budget envelope is report-only. Nothing in dispatch caps subagent count, depth or cost: a cap is containment and needs a ruled interview.

A research or mechanical lane routed to fable warns; escalation requires explicit operator justification. The cade.delegate.* roots carry that justification (TIN-7125 0a1924b3): Fable orchestrates those jobs and never runs their units.

Every model class a persona routes to, other than the operator, has an explicit seat record in seats; a seat never appears in the default personas of a persona that excludes its model class, and never serves a persona it lists as forbidden.

Per-agent and per-lane model choice follows this policy and names the seat model_id. The harness-wide default model stays provider-managed: pinning fable, opus, sonnet or haiku globally still needs an explicit host-level justification.

A harness seat may only receive tasks listed in its own delegable_tasks. It never owns the operator WORD/ratification leg and never owns the adversarial-refutation-of-record; harness output is evidence for the fable synthesis seat or the Opus merge gate. The gated-worker seat's output is work product whose external acts wait for a GO. It is never the ruling and never gates a merge. A lane routed to a harness seat therefore carries evidentiary work only.

Harness dispatch goes through the lab-managed bounded launchers named in the seat's dispatch_surface (the pi-* wrappers). A seat whose surface is a transport, such as an swb recipient, names the fixed launcher behind it in launcher, and the receiver calls only that launcher. Never execute a raw agent binary as a dispatch or probe surface.

When the operator asks to fan out, decompose the work into parallel concurrent workflow lanes, never one serial workflow. Each lane return is a Fable-operator interview checkpoint — live re-planning plus HITL ratification of merges and priorities — which a serial handoff suppresses.

harness_seats.dispatch_surface: lab-managed bounded pi-* launchers (never raw binaries)
harness_seats.purpose: Bounded technical-review harness seat. Fable delegates GitHub PR review, review commentary, and mechanical code-quality output here and reads the result back as evidence.

harness_seats.purpose: This IS the Kimi reviewer lane: Kimi rides the pi harness because the native kimi CLI has no dispatch envelope. Same bounded technical-review envelope and same evidentiary-only posture as the pi seat.

harness_seats.launcher: cade-job: the lab-managed fixed launcher the swb receiver calls (never a raw binary)
harness_seats.model_lane: anthropic/cade@xoxd.ai: the root seat comes from the cade.dispatch resolver and each unit's seat from cade.dispatch.units
harness_seats.purpose: Cade's job seat (TIN-7125). Cade sends a whole cade.delegate.* job here as a cade.dispatch/v1 envelope. A Claude Code session signed in to cade@xoxd.ai runs it under its own config dir, fans out subagents per unit and returns a cade.dispatch.receipt/v1 receipt.

lanes.purpose: Umbrella orchestration, cross-lane synthesis, architecture, and decision framing for the operator.
Advisory code and design review alongside the operator. It never gates a merge: the merge gate is mythos.gate.review on Opus.
Purple-team and refutation passes over synthesized findings before they reach the operator.
Implementation that lands on a default branch or a release. Opus 5.5 by default.
Independent merge-gating review. Runs on Opus 5.5 and never falls back to Sonnet. A Sonnet first pass or a harness review is evidence for it, never the gate.

Security-sensitive code, credentials paths and trust-boundary changes. Under the budget fallback Sonnet may write the code; the merge waits for an Opus review and live credentials wait for Opus or the operator.
Cluster and host acts: deploys, switches, migrations and anything that mutates shared infra. Never falls back to Sonnet: it waits for Opus or goes to the operator.
Drafts, non-merging prototypes and write-ups that a critical lane or the operator will finish.
First-pass review that narrows findings before the Opus merge gate.
Parallel domain recon across repos, docs, and infra.
Deep Linear initiative/project/issue exploration.
Web sweeps: specs, releases, ecosystem discussion.
File, directory, and config locators and inventories.
Polling CI and queues. Summarising logs.

Technical review delegated to a harness seat: GitHub PR review and review commentary, returned as adversarial_review_pass evidence for the fable synthesis seat. For a merge it is evidence for the Opus gate on mythos.gate.review, never the gate. Kimi rides pi-k3 on the identical envelope. Never the operator WORD leg.

Mechanical code-quality output delegated to a harness seat: lint-shaped findings, structural nits and checklist sweeps over a diff. Evidence only. The ruling stays with the operator, the fable seat and, for a merge, the Opus gate.

personas.doctrine: Fast synthesis and review seat. Avoid taking over bulk implementation or verification hammering unless explicitly asked. Never run adversarial, purple-team, or red-team analysis.
personas.purpose: Synthesis, architecture, and engineering judgment; the second engineer in the room.

personas.doctrine: Fable leads, others work (TIN-7125 0a1924b3). Fable plans, fans out and synthesizes. It never runs a unit itself. Workers are Sonnet or Haiku for research and bulk work, and Opus for code, gates and every adversarial, red-team, purple-team or deep-iteration unit at any depth. Bulk execution stays forbidden to fable. No mythos.* lane uses this persona.
personas.purpose: Root of a Cade delegated job: plan the job, pick each unit's model and synthesize the result. Only cade.delegate.* lanes use this persona.

personas.doctrine: Rely on Opus 5.5 or the operator personally. A merge-gating review runs on Opus. When Opus quota is exhausted the opus-quota-exhausted fallback lets Sonnet continue mythos.implement.merge and mythos.gate.security only. Their merges wait for an Opus review. The downgraded lane never runs a host act or a credential change. The downgrade is recorded in the receipt. mythos.gate.review and mythos.act.host never fall back: they wait for Opus or go to the operator. Never fable or haiku.
personas.purpose: Mission-critical execution and verification: implementation that merges, merge-gating review, security-sensitive code plus cluster and host acts.

personas.doctrine: Route to Opus 5.5 or the operator personally. Never route to fable. Prompt the skeptic to refute, not to agree. The budget fallback does not cover this persona: when Opus quota is exhausted the refutation-of-record waits or goes to the operator.
personas.purpose: Adversarial, purple-team, red-team, refutation, and deep-iteration verification lanes.

personas.doctrine: Fan out wide and return dense structured reports. Escalate model class with task depth: haiku for locators, sonnet for pattern extraction and broad recon, opus for the deepest research lanes. Use haiku and sonnet freely here. Kimi K3.1 Pro never takes this persona: Cade research runs on cade-research.
personas.purpose: Wide research, deep Linear exploration, web sweeps, multi-repo recon.

personas.doctrine: Sonnet 5.5 by default; use it freely. Output is a draft or a first pass. It never stands in for a merge-gating review and never merges on its own. Kimi K3.1 Pro never takes this persona: Cade drafts run on cade-drafting.
personas.purpose: Drafting, non-merging prototypes and first-pass review ahead of an Opus gate.

personas.doctrine: Cheapest lane. Keep prompts narrow and mechanical; return raw structured data.
personas.purpose: Locators, inventories, shallow greps, format conversions, polling, log summaries, checklist execution.

personas.doctrine: Kimi K3.1 Pro by default, with Opus 5.5 as the alternate, within the custody the child's parent home admits. Research returns evidence to the orchestrator. No mythos.* lane uses this persona: engineering research stays on the research persona.
personas.purpose: Cade's public market, competitor and lead research. Only cade.* lanes use this persona.

personas.doctrine: Kimi K3.1 Pro by default, with Opus 5.5 as the alternate, within the custody the child's parent home admits. Drafts only: anything sent goes through the daily batch confirm or Jess's confirm. No mythos.* lane uses this persona: engineering drafts stay on the drafting persona.
personas.purpose: Cade's proposals, briefs and other business drafts. Only cade.* lanes use this persona.

personas.doctrine: Opus 5.5 by default. Kimi K3.1 Pro is a permitted alternate where the lane's custody admits it. Output is a draft or a recommendation. Pricing, commitments, contracts and brand claims move to cade.critical. External acts wait for Jess's confirm.
personas.purpose: Business work for Cade: offers, partnerships, pipeline analysis and operating plans short of a commitment.

personas.doctrine: Kimi K3.1 Pro by default on public custody, with Opus 5.5 as the alternate. Drafts only: outreach and posts ship through the daily batch confirm, and other external sends wait for Jess's confirm.
personas.purpose: Marketing for Cade: copy, posts, campaign drafts and outreach drafts.

personas.doctrine: Opus 5.5 by default. Kimi K3.1 Pro is a permitted alternate on ops custody. It assembles the daily batch and never sends it. Spending, external sends and host acts wait for Jess's confirm.
personas.purpose: CEO operations for Cade: obligations, digests, scheduling preparation and assembling the daily batch.

personas.doctrine: Review is evidence, not authority. It never blocks, never gates a merge and never stands in for Jess's approval or a batch confirm. A same-provider review is recorded as same-provider.
personas.purpose: Advisory cross-provider review of consequential Cade output. The reviewer runs on the provider other than the author's.

The Platform endpoint names the model kimi-k3.1-pro. It is forbidden: no seat runs here and no Platform key is used (SP-34, SPR-143). It is listed so a consumer can recognise and refuse it.

scarce_resources.notes: Operator SWE/systems-engineer attention. Limited. Spend on decisions, design, and verification of load-bearing claims.
Fable-class model tokens: expensive, not always available, can be slow, compute costly, token-limited. Spend on the synthesis seat and on the orchestrator root of cade.delegate.* jobs only.
Opus 5.5 subagent quota. Spend it on mission-critical lanes first. When it runs out the opus-quota-exhausted budget fallback applies (J81(e)).

seats.notes: Fable-class synthesis seat: umbrella orchestration, architecture, engineering judgment and advisory review alongside the operator. Never the adversarial or critical seat. Its review never gates a merge. It also roots cade.delegate.* jobs as orchestrator on the fable-orchestrator persona (TIN-7125). For those jobs its model id is a config value read from the cade@xoxd.ai account after login, never a value in this policy.

Opus 5.5 is the primary execution and verification seat (J81). It is the default for mission-critical lanes: implementation that merges, merge-gating and adversarial review, refutation-of-record, security-sensitive work plus cluster and host acts. It is also the deepest-research seat and the default escalation target whenever fable tokens must be protected.

Sonnet 5.5 is used freely for research sweeps, drafting, broad recon, non-merging prototypes and first-pass review. It is not the default for mission-critical lanes. It may continue mythos.implement.merge or mythos.gate.security only under the opus-quota-exhausted budget fallback. It never gates a merge.
Haiku 5.5 is the cheapest seat and is used freely for mechanical lanes: locators, inventories, shallow greps, format conversions, polling, log summaries and checklist execution.

Kimi K3.1 Pro (k3.1-pro) on the kimi-coding endpoint through the Kimi Code subscription. The Platform endpoint and any Platform key are forbidden. It serves research, drafting, business, marketing, CEO-ops and evidentiary review on the cade.* lanes that name it, through personas that only cade.* lanes use. No mythos.* lane resolves to a persona that lists kimi. It never gates a merge. It never owns the refutation-of-record, never carries the operator WORD leg and never runs a critical host act. It never serves confidential or health custody. As the Cade broker it routes requests to cade.* lanes and authors cade.dispatch/v1 envelopes. It gates nothing and never names a model (cade.broker).
